newsitem.title: USA: Owenings Corning earnings rise 8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Owenings Corning earnings rise 8 percent.

text.p: Owens Corning said Tuesday its earnings rose 8 percent in the first quarter as a result of strength in its roofing operations and global aquisitions it made in the last two years.
The glass composite and building materials giant said income rose to $42 million from $39 millon a year ago. Earnings per share were 76 cents, up from 73 cents in the same period last year.
Sales rose to $875 million from $849 million.
"The strength of our roofing business and our global acquisitions made during the last two years drove our results for the quarter," said Chairman Glen Hiner.
The buildings materials business showed a strong 21 percent growth in earnings, mostly from sales to contractors and remodelers, the Toledo, Ohio-based company said.
The building materials division sales in Europe grew 11 percent, due to successful aquisitions such as Polypan Nord, S.P.A., a manufacturer of foam insulation products, the company said.

Sales of composite materials were down 7 percent from the same period last year due to pricing weakness in Europe, inventory adjustments and price competition in the United States, the company said. Owens Corning stock was off 12.5 cents to $37.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
